headline: OCC issues supervisory framework for examiners evaluating banks' use of AI
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), which oversees large national banks, issued a supervisory framework to support its examiners in evaluating banks' use of AI. The OCC says examiners should not treat it as a separate and distinct risk category, and banks are not required to define a separate risk appetite for it. The OCC says the framework does not establish supervisory expectations for banks.
note: For risk teams, the framework points examiners at what an AI agent is allowed to do and what happens if it fails, which is a different question from how advanced the model is.

evidence.text: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) today issued a supervisory framework designed to support OCC examiners in evaluating banks’ 1 use of super intelligence (SI) 2 in normal-course business activities.
clarifies that examiners should not treat SI as a separate and distinct risk category, and banks are not required to define a separate SI risk appetite.
This supervisory framework does not establish supervisory expectations for banks.
emphasizes a bank’s control intensity could increase with the potential consequences of an SI agent's failure or misuse.

clarifies that a bank’s risk classification of SI use cases may be based on potential consequences, transfer of agency, and the degree of human oversight rather than the technical sophistication of the SI used.

The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, which oversees large national banks, issued what it said was the first-ever guidance for how examiners should probe banks’ AI usage, according to a copy of the document seen by Reuters.
